program:
Roads between towns, read from a file: how many towns, roads and parts; the cheapest network that joins them (Kruskal's method, with union-find); the farthest town; and, for each trip the file asks, the shortest route (Dijkstra's method), and for each near, the towns within so many km. The first program here built on Map and Set.
Prior art: Edsger W. Dijkstra, "A note on two problems in connexion with graphs" (1959); Joseph B. Kruskal, "On the shortest spanning subtree of a graph" (1956); Bernard A. Galler and Michael J. Fischer, "An improved equivalence algorithm" (1964). Keeping the frontier as an ordered set of (distance, town) pairs instead of a heap is the textbook variant that needs no decrease-key.
